newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The government is hoping to restore its traditional good relations with the union movement and offset the fallout from recent labour unrest by beginning 'social dialogue' on great and small issues, such as economic growth, and employment and social security.

--New proposals and planning are being developed in the crucial and under-utilised sector of privatisation. The government's economic team is now working on selling all the firms currently under the Organisation for Ailing Enterprises umbrella in the next two years and on privatisations in the National, Commercial and Agricultural Banks.
--A consortium of five construction companies looks set to take ownership of Andreas Cambas wines by the end of the month, sources say.
--Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, is facing serious problems as the Commission questions certain reforms and changes initiated by the government.

--The Greek economy looks certain to be taken hostage by the farmers again. Farmers yesterday laughed off the strong police presence on national roads and managed to set up the first - albeit shortlived - road blocks. There is intense concern in the market over the dimensions the second round of protests could take.
--The finance ministry has issued an information leaflet on how to complete and submit the E9 form on the declaration of all real estate.
--The government is putting into action a new, improved and three year privatisation programme that aims at restricting the role of the state in business activity and boosting state revenues.

--The development ministry's new draft bill on tourism foresees increased investment incentives for infrastructural projects, such as conference centres and golf courses, and increased subsisides for modernisation in small and big hotels.
--There are feverish talks under way within the government in an effort to find the formula which will permit the speedier absorption of EU funds in 1997.

--The social security and pensions issue will come to the fore today in Prime Minister Costas Simitis's meeting with National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou, Labour and Social Security Minister Miltiades Papaioannou and undersecretary Christos Protopapas, while the issue is also expected to be raised at the Cabinet meeting tomorrow. Sources say the inability of the state to continue to support pension funds under the current fiscal conditions will be the major focus.
--Despite the fanfare of the official inauguration earlier last month, natural gas distribution is still facing problems, originating mainly in the lack of coordination between ministries.

--The government's housecleaning of public utilities and organisatios (DEKOs) is now under way with National Economy and Finance Minister Papandoniou soon sending all DEKOs a management contract to sign with the government. Also in the mail for all DEKOS are the targets of the general budget, which, it is stressed, cannot be overshot in any instance.
--The state is planning the issue of 10-year bonds to help better service the debt and provide the market with new products. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
